title: Coasts 5: Coral Reefs and Mangroves
subject: Geography
description: Where coral reefs and mangroves are found, the 3 types of reef, why they matter, the threats they face and how they are managed.
author: Erick

cards.front: Between which latitudes are coral reefs found?
cards.back: 30°N and 30°S

cards.front: Name areas where coral reefs are found.
cards.back: Australia / Mexico / Indonesia / Madagascar
In tropical and sub-tropical regions, e.g. Indonesia, Australia, the Brazil coast, Madagascar and Mexico.

cards.front: What conditions do coral reefs need?
cards.back: Warm, shallow, clear, salty water with plenty of sunlight.

cards.front: Coral reefs are often described as the...
cards.back: Rainforests of the sea
A reef that grows right next to the shore.
A reef separated from the shore by a wide, deep lagoon (e.g. the Great Barrier Reef).
A ring-shaped reef around a lagoon, left behind where a volcanic island has sunk.

cards.front: Name the type of coral reef labelled A.
cards.back: Fringing reef
cards.imageAlt: The three types of coral reef labelled A, B and C

cards.front: Name the type of coral reef labelled B.
cards.back: Barrier reef
cards.imageAlt: The three types of coral reef labelled A, B and C

cards.front: Name the type of coral reef labelled C.
cards.back: Atoll
cards.imageAlt: The three types of coral reef labelled A, B and C

cards.back: Although they cover a small area of the ocean, they provide diverse habitats for huge numbers of fish and other marine species.
Fishing communities depend on their fish, and tourism (e.g. diving and snorkelling) brings in billions of dollars a year and creates jobs.

cards.front: How do coral reefs protect the coast?
cards.back: They act as natural barriers, absorbing wave energy before it reaches the coast.
They provide diverse wildlife habitats and sheltered nursery grounds where young fish grow before moving into deeper water.
Fishing communities rely on them for food.

cards.front: How do mangroves protect the coast?
cards.back: Their roots trap sediment and reduce erosion, and they absorb wave energy, which limits flooding and damage to settlements during storms.

cards.front: How do mangroves help fight climate change?
cards.back: They absorb and store large amounts of carbon (CO₂), produce oxygen, and improve water quality by filtering pollutants.

cards.front: What is the most serious threat to coral reefs and mangroves?
cards.back: Climate change
Rising sea temperatures cause the organisms that make up coral to die off, leaving it white.

cards.front: How do storms threaten reefs and mangroves?
cards.back: Storms add sediment over reefs, damaging the coral, and disrupt the sediment deposition that mangroves need to develop.
The ocean becoming more acidic; along with warming oceans, scientists see it as a main threat to reefs.

cards.front: How does pollution threaten coral reefs?
cards.back: Pollution from agriculture, sewage and urban development reduces water quality and smothers coral with sediment. Extra nutrients cause excessive algae growth.
Pollution killing the wildlife, people removing and harvesting the mangrove wood, and urban development (resorts, ports and housing).

cards.front: Other human pressures on coral reefs and mangroves
cards.back: Overfishing, destructive fishing practices and poorly managed tourism.
Areas where damaging activities are restricted so ecosystems can recover naturally.
Separating tourism, fishing and conservation activities into different areas.
Taking pieces of coral that have been bleached and moving them to a safer place to regrow (restoring damaged reefs).
Making mangrove protected areas, water quality (pollution) control, and replanting mangroves.

questions.question: Between which latitudes are coral reefs found?
questions.explanation: Coral reefs are found between 30°N and 30°S.

questions.question: What causes coral bleaching?
questions.explanation: Rising sea temperatures from climate change cause bleaching, where the coral organisms die off.

questions.question: Which is a way mangroves protect the coast?
options: They add nutrients to the sea
questions.explanation: Mangrove roots trap sediment and absorb wave energy, reducing erosion and flooding.

questions.question: Which reef type is a ring around a lagoon with no island in the middle?
questions.explanation: An atoll is a ring of reef left when a volcanic island sinks.

questions.question: Separating tourism, fishing and conservation into different areas is called...
questions.explanation: Zoning separates activities so damaging ones are kept away from sensitive areas.
